fitReason: The current Cornell AR Lab combines robot perception and learned grasping with real field platforms; its newer foundation-model projects provide a relevant CS-to-robotics application area.

physicalEvidence.summary: The 2026 bin-picking author manuscript reports a real UR10 with Schunk WSG-50 and eye-in-hand D435i. A synthetic-data-trained CNN predicts segmentation, grasp confidence and depth, followed by analytical grasp planning. August 2026 disease-diagnosis work evaluates images collected by an Amiga-derived field robot; it is offline perception evaluation, not closed-loop MLLM robot control.

shortVisit.summary: The live Cornell lab page welcomes visiting researchers and students through formal exchange or fellowship programs. This is a conditional route, with no duration, self-funded exception or summer 2027 capacity stated.

unknowns: Xiang moved from NC State to Cornell in August 2025; use the Cornell contact and rules. The bin-picking preprint and field-image collection date to 2025, and current Cornell ownership of the UR10 is unverified, so physical evidence is capped at 20. Field-data accuracy is vulnerable to temporal leakage acknowledged by the authors. CALS distinguishes student Intern Paid/Unpaid or nondegree graduate status from terminal-degree scholar/fellow titles; the lab’s formal exchange/fellowship condition must be clarified rather than replaced by a self-funding assumption.

Summer 2027 acceptance, mentor capacity, exact dates, funding, visitor appointment, and applicable university/immigration approvals remain unconfirmed. Self-funding alone does not establish eligibility.
